intent_record.intent_summary: Refreshes the garbage collection timestamp during connection addition to maintain accurate cleanup scheduling logic.
intent_record.what: Inserted an assignment of the current kernel time (jiffies) cast to u32 into the list->last_gc field within the __nf_conncount_add function.
intent_record.how: Updates the recorded timestamp for the last garbage collection operation immediately after processing a connection, ensuring the cleanup scheduler reflects the most recent list activity.

intent_record.what: Removed the assignment of the current jiffies value to the list's last_gc field within the __nf_conncount_add function.
intent_record.how: Prevents the garbage collection timestamp from being reset on every new connection addition, ensuring the garbage collection timer is not artificially extended by connection churn.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement increments the connection count without proper bounds checking. According to the evidence, this occurs at line 251 in the critical path for incrementing connection counts. Without validation of the count value before incrementing, this can lead to integer overflow when the counter reaches its maximum value, allowing attackers to trigger denial-of-service conditions through unbounded memory consumption.
